links.outcome: Patient functional outcomes and satisfaction, AI agent vs doctor-led care in RCT
links.effect: AI group had significantly better knee function (IKDC), physical health (PCS), and satisfaction at 1 and 3 months (all p<0.05); differences not significant at 6 months (p>0.05).
links.quote: At 1 and 3 months, the AI group achieved significantly better outcomes in knee function (IKDC), physical health (PCS), and overall satisfaction (all p < 0.05).

links.outcome: AI agent response speed, quality and accuracy compared with physician communication
links.effect: AI responded faster (0.5±0.6 vs 358±47.5 min, p<0.05) with higher perceived quality but slightly lower accuracy (93.9% vs 98.1%, p<0.05).
links.quote: The AI system responded far more rapidly (0.5 ± 0.6 vs. 358 ± 47.5 min, p < 0.05) and provided feedback of higher perceived quality, though with slightly reduced accuracy (93.9% vs. 98.1%, p < 0.05).

screen.reason: Randomized controlled trial evaluating the deployment of a GPT-4-powered conversational agent directly with postoperative orthopedic patients versus routine doctor-led care via WeChat.
